title: Junctional tachycardia
summary: A focus in the AV junction fires fast. It drives the ventricles normally and the atria backwards.

events.label: Junctional focus
events.caption: A focus at the lower end of the AV node fires, here 120 times a minute, and overrides the sinus node.
events.ecg: No P wave precedes the QRS.

events.label: Ventricles
events.caption: The impulse goes down the His bundle, so the ventricles are activated in the normal way and the QRS is narrow.

events.label: Atria backwards
events.caption: The impulse also travels back up through the AV node to the atria. The atria are activated from the AV junction, so the P wave is inverted and falls near the QRS.
events.ecg: A retrograde (inverted) P wave just after the QRS, or buried in it.

teaching_points: Junctional tachycardia arises in or near the AV node and His bundle, usually with a narrow QRS.
The atria are activated retrogradely, so P waves are inverted in the inferior leads and may be hidden in the QRS.
Unlike AVNRT it does not need a premature beat to start and is not a circuit.
